scenario_text: Table 6 has three guests. Order O-862 includes iced tea for seat 1, a shared crab dip for the table, and entrees of steak for seat 1, trout for seat 2, and pasta for seat 3. The order is confirmed. The iced tea and crab dip are queued; all three entrees are held until the shared crab dip has been served. Items progress from queued to in prep to ready to served. After the dip is served, the entrees may move from held to queued, then proceed through the normal preparation and service states. All items must be delivered to the specified seat or, for the dip, to the table to share.

validation_steps.action_summary: Start the iced tea for Table 6, seat 1.
Mark the prepared iced tea ready.
Serve the iced tea to seat 1 and mark it served.
Start the shared crab dip for Table 6.
Mark the prepared crab dip ready.
Serve the ready crab dip to Table 6 and mark it served.
Release all three entrees after the shared dip has been served.
Start the steak, trout, and pasta from queued status.
Mark all three prepared entrees ready.
Serve the steak to seat 1, trout to seat 2, and pasta to seat 3.

proposed_workflow_text: 1. The bar starts the iced tea for Table 6, seat 1. 2. The bar marks the iced tea ready. 3. The server delivers the iced tea to seat 1 and marks it served. 4. The kitchen starts the shared crab dip for Table 6. 5. The kitchen marks the dip ready. 6. The server delivers the dip to the table and marks it served. 7. The expediter releases the three held entrees to queued status. 8. The kitchen starts the steak, trout, and pasta. 9. The kitchen marks all three entrees ready. 10. The server delivers each entree to its assigned seat and marks it served.

scenario_text: Table 14 has two guests. Order O-731 assigns tomato soup and roast chicken to seat 1, and garden salad and salmon to seat 2. The order is confirmed. Both starters are queued; both entrees are held. Each entree may be released to the kitchen only after the starter for the same seat has been served. Item states progress from queued to in prep to ready to served; a held entree moves to queued when released.

validation_steps.action_summary: Start the tomato soup for Table 14, seat 1, and the garden salad for seat 2.
Mark both starters ready after preparation.
Serve each ready starter to its assigned seat.
Release both held entrees after the corresponding starters have been served.
Start the roast chicken and salmon from queued status.
Mark both prepared entrees ready.
Serve the roast chicken to seat 1 and the salmon to seat 2.

proposed_workflow_text: 1. The kitchen starts the tomato soup for Table 14, seat 1, and the garden salad for Table 14, seat 2. 2. The kitchen marks both starters ready. 3. The server delivers each starter to its assigned seat and marks it served. 4. After both starters are served, the expediter releases the roast chicken and salmon tickets from held to queued. 5. The kitchen starts both entrees. 6. The kitchen marks both entrees ready. 7. The server delivers the roast chicken to seat 1 and the salmon to seat 2, marking each served.

scenario_text: Table 8 has two guests. Order R-204 assigns braised beef to seat 1, roasted potatoes as that entree's side, and mushroom risotto to seat 2. A separate order, R-205, is for chicken piccata at Table 9, seat 1. The beef and risotto are queued; the potatoes are held until the beef is marked ready. Entree states progress from queued to in prep to ready to served. The potatoes may move from held to queued only after the beef reaches ready status. Tickets must remain associated with their original table, seat, and order.

validation_steps.action_summary: Start the braised beef for R-204, Table 8, seat 1.
Relabel the in-prep beef ticket as R-205 for Table 9, seat 1, and route it to that station.
validation_steps.violation_explanation: The beef belongs to R-204 at Table 8, seat 1. Relabeling it as R-205 assigns the item to the wrong order and table.

validation_steps.action_summary: Release the roasted potatoes from held to queued while the beef is still in prep.
validation_steps.violation_explanation: The potatoes may be released only after the associated beef is marked ready; it is still in prep, so the dependency and required state transition have not been satisfied.

violation_summary: Step 2 misassigns the Table 8 beef ticket to the Table 9 order. Step 3 releases the potatoes before the beef is ready.
proposed_workflow_text: 1. The kitchen starts the braised beef for Table 8, seat 1, moving it from queued to in prep. 2. The expediter relabels that in-prep beef ticket as the Table 9, seat 1 chicken piccata order and routes it to that station without changing its in-prep status. 3. While the beef is still in prep, the expediter releases the roasted potatoes from held to queued.
